items.title: Astronomers crack two 50-year stellar mysteries in rapid succession

featured_image.name: Supercomputers expose how spinning red giants remix their cores

items.description: Two long-standing puzzles in stellar astrophysics have been cracked in rapid succession, with researchers announcing breakthroughs on both the enigmatic surface chemistry of red giant stars and the origin of unusual X-rays from one of the night sky's most visible stars.

items.title: Study finds Europe's last Neanderthals descended from one small group

featured_image.name: Shocking New Study Reveals the Exact Moment Neanderthals Started to  Disappear

items.description: Europe's last Neanderthals descended from a single small population that survived harsh Ice Age conditions by retreating to a climate refuge in what is now southwestern France, according to a study published this week in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences. The finding adds to a growing body of genetic evidence showing that severe losses of diversity plagued Neanderthal populations long before their final disappearance roughly 40,000 years ago.

items.title: UN report finds freshwater fish migrations collapsing worldwide

featured_image.name: Migratory freshwater fish decline 76 percent since 1970, new ...

items.description:
Some of the longest and most important animal migrations on Earth are happening beneath the surface of the world's rivers — and many are rapidly collapsing. That is the finding of a major new assessment released on Monday at the UN's Convention on the Conservation of Migratory Species (CMS) conference in Campo Grande, Brazil, which identifies hundreds of freshwater fish species in urgent need of international protection.[1][2]

The Global Assessment of Migratory Freshwater Fishes, described as the most comprehensive overview ever assembled of migratory freshwater fish conservation needs, found that populations of migratory freshwater fish have declined by roughly 81 percent since 1970. Nearly all — 97 percent — of the 58 CMS-listed migratory fish species are now threatened with extinction.[2][3][1]

items.title: Foreign investors pull $50B from Asian stocks in record March exodus

featured_image.name: Asia stock rout deepens as markets brace for energy shock ...

items.description: Global financial markets remain gripped by volatility as the war between the United States, Israel, and Iran enters its fourth week, with oil prices climbing back above $100 a barrel and foreign investors fleeing Asian equities at a pace not seen since the 2008 financial crisis. Data from LSEG shows approximately $50 billion in net foreign equity outflows from South Korea, Taiwan, India, and Southeast Asian markets throughout March, positioning 2026 for the largest monthly capital flight from the region in nearly two decades.[1][2]

items.title: Business activity slumps across Europe, India and Asia amid Iran war

featured_image.name: Eurozone factory PMI slips back to contraction | trans.info

items.description: Business activity across the eurozone, India and parts of Asia slowed sharply in March as the war in the Middle East drove energy prices higher and sapped demand, according to flash purchasing managers' index data released Tuesday by S&P Global. The surveys, conducted between March 12 and March 20, offer the first broad snapshot of economic damage since the U.S. and Israel launched strikes on Iran on February 28.[1][2]

items.title: Japan to release 53M barrels from national oil reserves starting March 26

featured_image.name: Tokyo told national oil reserve site to prepare for release amid Iran  crisis, Japan lawmaker says | Reuters

items.description:
Japan will begin releasing crude oil from its national petroleum reserves on March 26, trade and industry minister Ryosei Akazawa announced Monday, as the country scrambles to cushion the blow of supply disruptions caused by the near-closure of the Strait of Hormuz during the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran.[1][2]

The release of approximately 8.5 million kiloliters — roughly 53 million barrels — from 11 stockpiling bases nationwide marks the start of a broader drawdown totaling about 80 million barrels, equivalent to 45 days of supply. Domestic refiners Eneos, Idemitsu, Cosmo Oil, and Taiyo Oil will each receive volumes equivalent to nearly one month of requirements.[3][1]

items.title: U.S. stock futures slip as Iran denies peace talks with Washington

featured_image.name: Wall Street retreats from record closing highs as economic ...

items.description: U.S. stock futures dipped in early trading on Tuesday as conflicting signals over potential peace talks between Washington and Tehran rattled investors and reversed much of the previous session's gains. Dow futures fell roughly 0.09%, while S&P 500 and Nasdaq futures edged lower, reflecting deepening uncertainty over the trajectory of the nearly four-week-old war in Iran.[1][2]

items.title: SMFG preparing possible takeover of Jefferies, FT reports

featured_image.name: SMFG Mulls Raising Jefferies Stake to About 20% as Ties ...

items.description:
Sumitomo Mitsui Financial Group is working on plans for a potential takeover of Jefferies Financial Group, according to a Financial Times report published Tuesday that sent Jefferies shares sharply higher in premarket trading.[1][2]

SMFG, Japan's second-largest lender, has assembled a small internal team tasked with monitoring conditions and positioning the bank to act should Jefferies' depressed share price present a compelling opportunity, the FT reported, citing people familiar with the matter. Jefferies shares climbed roughly 9.5% in U.S. premarket trading on Tuesday, while Frankfurt-listed shares had already jumped 6% following the report. SMFG shares closed up 2.78% in Tokyo.[3][4][2][5]

items.title: Iran fires missiles at Israel as IRGC rejects Trump's peace talk claims

featured_image.name: Iran says missiles fired at Israel in response to assassinations

items.description: Iran fired several missile salvos at Israel overnight Monday into Tuesday, striking areas in Tel Aviv, Haifa, and northern Israel, even as President Donald Trump insisted that "very strong" peace talks with Tehran were underway — claims Iranian officials flatly denied.

items.title: Iran hits Tel Aviv with cluster missiles as war enters fourth week

featured_image.name: Tel Aviv residents assess damage after Iranian missile strike kills one

items.description: Iran fired fresh waves of missiles into central Israel on Tuesday, striking areas near Tel Aviv and Haifa with cluster munitions, as Tehran dismissed President Donald Trump's claims of ongoing peace negotiations as "fake news" — a contradiction that sent oil prices surging after a brief reprieve.

items.title: China mapping ocean floor for submarine warfare, Reuters finds

featured_image.name: China is mapping the ocean floor as it prepares for ...

items.description: China is conducting a vast undersea mapping and monitoring operation across the Pacific, Indian, and Arctic oceans, building detailed knowledge of marine conditions that naval experts say would be crucial for waging submarine warfare against the United States and its allies, according to a Reuters investigation published Monday.[1][2]

items.title: Sunken Soviet sub is leaking radioactive material, study finds

featured_image.name: A sunken one-of-a-kind Soviet nuclear sub appears to be leaking ...

items.description: Two Cold War-era nuclear hazards — a cracking concrete dome in the Marshall Islands and a corroding Soviet submarine on the floor of the Norwegian Sea — are drawing renewed scientific attention as researchers document ongoing radioactive releases into the world's oceans.

items.title: Magnitude 7.6 earthquake strikes near Tonga; no tsunami threat

featured_image.name: Magnitude 7.6 earthquake rattles Neiafu, Tonga

items.description: A magnitude 7.6 earthquake struck near Tonga in the South Pacific on Tuesday, according to the United States Geological Survey, but the deep tremor prompted no tsunami warning and there were no immediate reports of damage or casualties.

items.title: AWS Bahrain region disrupted by drones for second time this month

featured_image.name: Drone strikes damage Amazon data centres in UAE and Bahrain ...

items.description:
Amazon said on Monday that its Amazon Web Services cloud computing region in Bahrain has "been disrupted" due to drone activity, marking the second time the facility has been hit since the start of the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran earlier this month.[1][2]

The disruption was first reported by Reuters, with an Amazon spokesperson confirming that the outage stemmed from drone activity in the area. Amazon said it is helping to migrate customers to alternate AWS regions while it works to recover, though the company did not disclose the extent of the damage or provide a timeline for restoration.[2][1]

"As this situation evolves and, as we have advised before, we request those with workloads in the affected regions continue to migrate to other locations," Amazon said in a statement Monday night.[2]

items.title: ISS images of Russian missile strike on Kyiv verified by analysts

featured_image.name: ISS captures images of Russian missile strike on Kyiv from space

items.description:
Images taken from the International Space Station appear to show Russian ballistic missiles streaking toward Kyiv and being intercepted by Ukrainian air defenses, offering a rare space-based view of the war that has gripped analysts and the public alike.

The photographs, captured by an ISS-mounted camera on December 27, 2025, show two luminous trails moving from the northeast toward the Ukrainian capital before vanishing amid bursts of explosions in and around the city. The footage was compiled into a timelapse by Italian space enthusiast Riccardo Rossi of the AstronautiCAST YouTube channel and first published on February 23, 2026, quickly spreading through Ukrainian open-source intelligence channels on the eve of the war's fourth anniversary.[1][2][3]

items.title: Oil prices swing as Iran denies Trump's claim of war talks

featured_image.name: Trump to postpone strikes on Iranian power plants for five days

items.description: Oil prices swung wildly on Monday as President Donald Trump claimed the United States held "productive conversations" with Iran aimed at ending the four-week-old war, only for Tehran to flatly deny any negotiations took place. The conflicting signals sent crude benchmarks tumbling from recent highs before partially recovering, while Wall Street rallied on hopes for a diplomatic resolution.

items.title: Australia, EU poised to finalize free trade deal after nearly a decade of talks

featured_image.name: EU and Australia strike free trade deal after years of talks

items.description: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen arrived in Australia on Monday for a three-day visit aimed at concluding a free trade agreement that has been under negotiation since 2018. Von der Leyen is set to meet Prime Minister Anthony Albanese in Canberra on Tuesday, with both sides signaling they are close to finalizing a deal that would also include a new security and defense partnership.[1][2]

items.title: Iran parliament speaker Ghalibaf ID'd as Trump negotiation partner

featured_image.name: thumbs_b_c_82d6fe7a4bd6e069b97c337d7a26ff5e.jpg?v=103723

items.description:
Iran's parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf has been identified by U.S. and Israeli sources as the Iranian official at the center of talks with American envoys, even as Tehran flatly denies any negotiations are taking place and Ghalibaf himself dismissed the reports as "fake news."

President Donald Trump announced Monday that he was ordering a five-day pause on planned strikes against Iran's power plants and energy infrastructure, saying the U.S. had held "very good and productive conversations" with Iranian counterparts over the preceding two days. Trump said his special envoy Steve Witkoff and son-in-law Jared Kushner had been in discussions with "a top person" in Iran but refused to identify the individual, saying he did not want that person to be killed.[1][2][3][4]

items.title: Colombian military plane crashes after takeoff, killing at least one

featured_image.name: Colombia military plane crash: 110 soldiers on board

items.description:
A Colombian Air Force C-130 Hercules transport plane carrying 125 people crashed moments after takeoff Monday morning in the country's remote southern Amazon region, killing at least one person, injuring 77 others, and leaving more than 40 still unaccounted for as rescue operations continued into the evening.

The aircraft went down about two kilometers from the airport in Puerto Leguízamo, a municipality in the Amazonian province of Putumayo near the borders of Peru and Ecuador, according to Defense Minister Pedro Sánchez, who disclosed the crash on X and called it a "tragic accident." The Lockheed Martin-built plane was transporting 114 soldiers and 11 crew members to another city in Putumayo province when it encountered an unspecified problem and plunged to the ground.[1][2][3][4]

items.title: Claude can now point, click and navigate your Mac like a human user

featured_image.name: Anthropic Says New AI Model Is Better at Using Computers ...

items.description: Anthropic is rolling out new capabilities that allow its Claude AI to directly control Mac computers, pointing, clicking, and navigating applications the way a human user would. The update, arriving March 23 for Claude Pro and Max subscribers as a research preview, brings computer-use features to both Claude Cowork and Claude Code on macOS.[1]
